around.headline: Bengaluru mother battling postpartum depression drowns twin infant daughters
around.summary: A Bengaluru woman drowned her four-month-old IVF-conceived twin daughters and attempted suicide while battling postpartum depression; police have filed an FIR, per Rediff, ThePrint and The New Indian Express. If you or someone around a new mother notices persistent sadness, withdrawal or dark thoughts, don't wait it out — involve family early or call the government's KIRAN mental health helpline (1800-599-0019).
around.source: Rediff, ThePrint, The New Indian Express

around.headline: 'Operation Mukta' crackdown picks up Bengali speakers as 31 Bangladeshi nationals deported
around.summary: A TNM ground report says Bengaluru's 'Operation Mukta' crackdown has led to Bengali-speaking residents being picked up by police, while separately 31 Bangladeshi nationals were arrested and sent to West Bengal's Malda for deportation this week, per The Times of India and mid-day.com. If you or someone you know speaks Bengali, keep ID and residence proof on hand when out and about.
around.source: The Times of India, mid-day.com, TNM

around.headline: Traffic advisory: five major flyovers to see restrictions
around.summary: A fresh travel advisory flags five major Bengaluru flyovers for upcoming traffic restrictions, per Travel and Leisure Asia. Check the advisory before your commute if you regularly use flyovers to avoid getting stuck.

around.headline: Metro Pink Line's 7.5-km stretch awaits two more clearances
around.summary: The Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch of the Pink Line is physically ready, but two clearances are still pending before the expected September launch, per The Times of India, The Hindu and Daily Pioneer. Commuters on that corridor should hold off on firm plans until the official opening date is announced.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu, Daily Pioneer

around.headline: GBA bans PoP Ganesh idols ahead of Gowri-Ganesha festival
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has banned Plaster of Paris Ganesh idols ahead of the Gowri-Ganesha festival, per Udayavani and ThePrint. If you're buying an idol this season, ask specifically for an eco-friendly clay one to avoid a last-minute swap or fine.

around.headline: Nepal flash-flood toll nears 1,250 as heavy-rain warnings continue
around.summary: Nepal's flash-flood death toll has climbed to near 1,250 with over 4,000 still missing, and IMD's heavy-to-extremely-heavy rainfall warnings tied to the same weather system remain in force, per The Hindu and BBC. It's part of why Bengaluru itself is looking at an 80% rain chance today — the same active system is feeding both.

street_smart.title: You get a WhatsApp message offering a well-paying work-from-home job — no interview needed. Before they 'onboard' you, the recruiter asks for a small, fully 'refundable' registration or security deposit via UPI to activate your employee ID. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No matching safety/scam incident in today's feeds (the closest, a repeat Facebook-impersonation arrest story, was already covered as this brief's street-smart scenario on Sept 2 evening). Falling back to the evergreen rotation: fake job offers & deposit fraud, which hasn't appeared as a scenario in the archive over the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The recruiter has a professional-sounding company name, a polished offer letter PDF, and points to a real-looking (but unofficial) careers portal link — the deposit is framed as standard 'onboarding formality' that gets refunded in your first salary.

choices.text: Don't pay anything — independently look up the company's official careers page or verified HR email/domain, and confirm the opening exists there before responding further.
choices.feedback: Correct. Legitimate employers never collect money from candidates for registration, training kits, or 'refundable' deposits at any stage. Verifying through a channel you found yourself — not one the recruiter handed you — is what actually confirms the job is real.

choices.text: Pay the small deposit since it's supposed to be refundable and the salary on offer is generous.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. There is no real job — the 'deposit' is the entire scam, dressed up as a formality to make it feel routine. Once paid, it's rarely refunded, and paying often invites more demands ('device fee', 'training fee') from the same recruiter.

choices.text: Ask the recruiter for the company's registration certificate or GST number first, and pay only after they send it.
choices.feedback: Risky. Certificates and GST numbers can be copied or faked just as easily as an offer letter — a document from the same source that's asking for money doesn't independently verify anything. Check the company through its own official website or a professional network instead.

choices.text: Skip the deposit but go ahead and share your bank account details so they can 'set up salary crediting' in advance.
choices.feedback: Risky. Not paying money is the right instinct, but handing over bank details upfront to an unverified recruiter still exposes you — some job scams use collected account details for further fraud. Verify the employer first, before sharing anything.

takeaways: A genuine employer never asks a candidate to pay — for registration, training kits, or a 'refundable' deposit — before or during hiring.
Verify any job offer through the company's own official careers page or a verified HR email domain, not just a WhatsApp/Telegram number or a link the recruiter sends you.
Report fake job offers to the national cyber-fraud helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, and flag the listing on whichever platform (LinkedIn, Naukri, WhatsApp) it came through.

quiz.question: Bengaluru Metro's Pink Line stretch nearing its September launch is still waiting on how many clearances, per today's reports?
quiz.why: The 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch is physically ready, but two clearances remain before it can open to the public.

quiz.question: Ahead of the Gowri-Ganesha festival, the Greater Bengaluru Authority has banned Ganesh idols made of what material?
quiz.why: PoP idols don't dissolve like clay ones and pollute lakes and water bodies when immersed, which is why civic bodies push eco-friendly clay idols instead.

quiz.question: Nepal's flash-flood death toll, per today's reports, has climbed to near what number?
quiz.why: Over 4,000 people are still reported missing, with the same weather system also triggering IMD's heavy-rain warnings across several Indian states.

quiz.question: India's Directive Principles of State Policy, which guide governance but aren't legally enforceable, were inspired by which country's constitution?
quiz.why: The Irish constitution's 'directive principles' were themselves modeled on Spain's, making India's borrowing a second-hand one.

quiz.question: Sunlight exposure helps the human body synthesize which essential vitamin?
quiz.why: UVB rays trigger vitamin D synthesis in skin, which is why indoor-heavy lifestyles in sunny cities like Bengaluru can still see deficiency.
